conventions.convention: The complex infinity matrix norm is the maximum absolute row sum, using complex moduli; its matrix dimensions are positive.
Uniform linear residual data bound I−RA and R(b−A x̂) in induced Euclidean norms for every admitted A and b; usable means q<1.
Residual and orthogonality bounds are uniform over a nonempty Hermitian family, with δ<1 and radius ρ+(M_A+M_Θ)τ.
Realification uses the block matrix [[X,−Y],[Y,X]], standard inner products linear in the first variable, and duplicates each Hermitian eigenvalue twice.
Inertia triples are ordered positive, negative, zero; the empty matrix has inertia (0,0,0).
Krawczyk existence uses inclusion in a nonempty closed box and a nonsingular preconditioner; uniqueness is per fixed system and requires the separate defect bound q<1.
Bisection eigenvalues are increasingly ordered; successful queries count eigenvalues strictly below the shift and exclude eigenvalues equal to the shift.
The bisection budget counts total queries across indices; blocked and budget-exhausted outputs preserve existing brackets.
The resolvent cover certifies invertibility and a uniform boundary norm bound only; it supplies neither contour topology nor an enclosed eigenvalue count.

load_bearing.statement: Usable uniform residual certificate data imply that every admitted Ax=b has a unique solution x_A(b) with ‖x_A(b)−x̂‖₂≤r/(1−q).
For n≥1 and residual and orthogonality certificate data for a nonempty Hermitian family, every increasing ordered eigenvalue satisfies |λ_k(A)−θ_(k)|≤ρ+(M_A+M_Θ)τ.
Realification respects compatible products and adjoints, preserves invertibility and operator 2-norms, and duplicates every Hermitian eigenvalue.
For Hermitian H=[[D,B*],[B,C]] with nonsingular Hermitian D, inertia(H)=inertia(D)+inertia(C−BD⁻¹B*), with coordinatewise addition.

Starting from a uniform eigenvalue bracket, midpoint updates using the stated exact counts below nonsingular shifts preserve each ordered eigenvalue enclosure; inconclusive queries leave the bracket unchanged, and s successful queries divide its initial width by 2^s.

Under the stated segment-to-disk cover and bounds e_j, δ_A, s_j, if q_j=e_j+s_j(r_j+δ_A)<1 for every disk, then zI−A is invertible throughout the supplied contour for every admitted A, with inverse infinity norm at most max_j s_j/(1−q_j).

For the stated nonempty families, closed complex rectangle box X, x₀∈X and nonsingular R, K*(X)⊆X gives a solution in X for every admitted pair; the additional uniform complex infinity defect bound q<1 gives uniqueness in X for each fixed pair.
For compatible complex matrices and vectors with positive dimensions, ‖Ax‖∞≤‖A‖∞,C‖x‖∞ and ‖AB‖∞,C≤‖A‖∞,C‖B‖∞,C.

concerns.concern: F3 says the algorithm 'checks RS=SR=I'. The cited algorithm instead admits input matrices 'with exact identities RS=SR=I'; its operational steps check interval evaluation, inclusion and the defect norm, but contain no inverse-witness check. The theorem remains sound on its admitted inputs, and Proof 1.1 correctly uses the supplied identity. F3 inaccurately describes an input condition as an executed check.

alerts.finding: In thm-orbital-stability-from-certified-floquet-multipliers, Proof 1.1 says 'while [F4] says a d×d characteristic polynomial has exactly d roots counted with multiplicity'. F4 actually cites lem-periodic-poincare-spectrum-matches-transverse-monodromy and describes the Poincare derivative spectrum for a least-period orbit. It does not state the quoted polynomial root-count proposition. The finite-dimensional root-count fact is standard, but this numbered citation attributes it to the wrong supplier.

seams_checked.note: The point certifier uses the operationwise no-underflow model and the rounded linear residual allowances, checks the dot-product denominator condition, and evaluates certificate bounds outward. It assumes no solver stability or unconditional range success.

The interval LDL certifier invokes only the exact midpoint branch with the same ordering, partition and threshold. Independent interval pivot and Schur-complement checks establish family inertia; midpoint failure supplies no singularity claim.

Finite rectangle DAG enclosures and outward norm calculations are used under their domain restrictions. Undefined or non-finite operations produce inconclusive statuses rather than finite certificates.
The Euclidean Neumann inverse-norm lemma applies the supplier to −E with norm below one and derives the quantitative bound locally. No nonnormal forward eigenvalue estimate is inferred.

Floquet counting uses the validator only for a uniform complex infinity resolvent bound. Polygon topology, quadrature error and argument-principle counting are supplied separately. The orbital-stability proof uses the complex infinity Neumann lemma with a strict defect bound.

This is retained reading context. The nonlinear Krawczyk items use their own real-box Brouwer, interval Jacobian and interval arithmetic suppliers; no strengthening of the batch's linear Krawczyk theorem was found.

Contour error and Padé certification retain the complex infinity norm and require the supplied resolvent cover. Cauchy-cycle topology and spectral containment remain explicit caller hypotheses; validator success is not treated as an eigenvalue count.

Golub–Welsch uses certified uniform linear residual balls for coefficient solves and the near-orthonormal certifier for all increasing ordered eigenvalues of the enclosing Hermitian Jacobi family. Proposal eigensolver output alone is not accepted as a certificate.
